facts.fact: Agence Ecofin says Mauritania has been connected to the ACE cable since 2011 and still depends heavily on it, with no fully operational alternative, so ACE outages disrupt internet nationwide; ACE is the single route in service.

note: Second cable (EllaLink, 200 Gbps, coastal section landed Nouadhibou 4 May 2026, commissioning expected January 2027) is not yet in service.

facts.fact: The EIB press release says Mauritania connected to the Africa Coast to Europe (ACE) submarine cable in 2010 (other sources say 2011), and that a contract for a second cable was awarded to Ellalink.

note: EIB financing record for the MEDUSA cable's Mauritania landing; it does not state the cable is in service.

facts.fact: EllaLink says it has built a new neutral cable landing station in Nouadhibou that lets Mauritania's national operators access the infrastructure via two diverse routes (landing marked 4 May 2026; the document does not say the branch is yet in service).

note: Branch landed 4 May 2026 but not stated to be in service, so no routes fact.

facts.fact: DatacenterDynamics reports that only one subsea cable currently lands in Mauritania, the ACE system at Nouakchott, in which International Mauritania Telecom is the Mauritanian participant.

note: The EllaLink branch is under construction (ready for service early 2027 per the document); date is the article's, as it gives no other.
Contract-stage release for a branch not yet built (service projected early 2027); no route in service and no access term for a Mauritanian station stated.

facts.fact: The ACE consortium says the ACE cable was put into service on 15 December 2012 and lists Nouakchott as one of its landing stations, the first international submarine cable to land in Mauritania.

note: Page is undated (published date is a staging proxy); the access statement is only that agreements are being put in place for other operators, not a fact.

facts.fact: Maroc Telecom's West Africa submarine cable (9,414 km) lands in Mauritania at Nouadhibou, its south segment operational from July 2021, per the deal record built from a Maroc Telecom press release.

note: One landing station (Nouadhibou) stated; no access terms stated.
Open access duty of SDIN covers the national backbone, not international landing or capacity; WARCIP aim and a tender for new-cable works are not in-service facts.

facts.fact: Maroc Telecom's completed (2020-2022) 5,700 km terrestrial fibre cable from Morocco through Mauritania, Mali and Burkina Faso to Niger lets the Moov Africa subsidiary in Mauritania reach international bandwidth over the Maroc Telecom network (Morocco side); the document gives only the year 2022 for completion and its own published date.

facts.fact: Ecofin Agency says the ACE submarine cable has connected Mauritania since 2011 and the country still depends heavily on this single system for international connectivity; a second cable began coastal installation on 4 May 2026 with service expected in January 2027.
Maroc Telecom's nine-month 2025 fact sheet lists, among Moov Mauritel's highlights for January-September 2025, the commissioning of the West Africa submarine cable landing station in Nouadhibou.

facts.fact: Moov Mauritel's BU WAC interconnection catalogue for 2025/2026, published on the regulator's site, says it runs the Mauritanian branch of the West Africa Cable submarine cable landing at the Nouadhibou terminal station, with capacity and IP transit sold to Marseille, Lisbon, Seville and Madrid.

The same catalogue, issued after ARE's non-objection under authorisation 221/2024/ARE/CNR/DTTP of 23 December 2024, offers dedicated capacity and IP transit on the WAC cable at published tariffs to Mauritanian operators, internet service providers and international clients.

note: A January 2024 general procurement notice lists planned acquisitions only; nothing is stated as delivered, procured or in service.
